gloss: it seems; it appears; it looks like

definitions.gloss: it seems; it appears; it looks like
definitions.explanation: Expresses the speaker's judgment or inference based on what they have observed or sensed. Indicates that something appears to be a certain way.
Used to make comparisons or similes, expressing that something resembles or is similar to something else.

definitions.gloss: in such a way that; so that
definitions.explanation: Used with verbs to express a desired manner or goal, indicating the way something should be done.

examples.english: It looks like it's going to rain.

notes:
One of the most versatile and frequently used expressions in Japanese. Written as {様|よう}だ when using kanji, though the hiragana form is more common. Attaches to the plain form of verbs, い-adjectives, な-adjective stems + な, and nouns + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- verb plain + ようだ: ⟦{来|く}る→来る：00254_kuru⟧ようだ (it seems they're coming)
- い-adjective + ようだ: ⟦{寒|さむ}い→寒い：00664_samui⟧ようだ (it seems cold)
- な-adjective + なようだ: ⟦{元気|げんき}→元気：00696_genki⟧なようだ (seems healthy)
- noun + ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ようだ: ⟦{春|はる}→春：00627_haru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ようだ (like spring)
- ように + verb: ⟦{聞|き}こえる→聞こえる：01229_kikoeru⟧ように⟦{話|はな}す→話す：00467_hanasu⟧ (speak so one can be heard)
- ように⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to make an effort to; to make sure to
- ように⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to come to; to become able to

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦みたい→みたい：10755_mitai⟧だ: colloquial equivalent of ようだ (sense 1 and 2); ようだ is more formal
- らしい: based on hearsay or indirect evidence, while ようだ is based on the speaker's own observation
- そうだ (appearance): based on visual impression of the moment, while ようだ involves more deliberate judgment
